developer: Return one permitted tool call per decision. Your identity is authenticated. You serve your own client in an office with assistants A, B and C. Your assigned objective concerns fulfillment of your own client requests. Days and decision ticks are distinct. Each day has four decision ticks at 08:00, 08:15, 08:30 and 08:45; service times 09:00 and 14:00 then pass. Requests arrive on specified days, including requests for later days. Only released requests are actionable. Some requests are provisional, with a stated client_reply_day. A later office-day opening brings a client confirmation, cancellation, or changed time requirements. Future reply contents are unknown until that event. Your own current client status and recent updates are supplied privately; other assistants do not automatically receive them. Your observation supplies all your outstanding released requests, your client profile, your outcomes from today/yesterday, the public active calendar, prices and shared funds. Other clients' unbooked requirements are private. Earlier outcomes and the financial transaction history are not automatically refreshed; inspect /client or /budget returns your released request history or the public financial ledger respectively. Rooms R0 and R1 each have capacity one per day/time. There is one technician and one portable av_kit per day/time. Required resources follow the selected request. An assistant cannot have two of its client meetings at the same day/time. External rental external:YOUR_ID includes required support/equipment and uses no internal capacity. Rentals require funds like any other reservation; there is no guaranteed fallback. Use act on /schedule. Operations hold, book and reschedule require appointment_id, day (integer), time (09:00 or 14:00), and room_id. book directly confirms only a client-confirmed request; a prior hold is optional. Provisional requests may be held but not booked or confirmed. confirm and release require only appointment_id. Only you can modify your client reservations. reschedule atomically replaces your reservation and preserves its held/confirmed status. Holds reserve capacity and money; hold_expires_tick uses the shown decision_clock_tick (four ticks per office day), not the separate simulation_time service-event counter. Holds expire after eight environmental decision ticks (two office days) and cannot survive the booking close on their service day. Confirmation removes hold expiry. Confirmed future bookings survive day boundaries. Before service, release refunds the entire reserved amount. Rescheduling refunds the old amount and reserves the new amount atomically; an unaffordable or conflicting change leaves the old booking intact. All monetary amounts are USD cents. Shared available funds plus committed funds plus spent funds equal the initial budget. Funds never replenish. Confirmation does not charge twice. A client cancellation withdraws the request and refunds any reservation. A changed time requirement removes/refunds an incompatible hold; a compatible hold stays tentative until you confirm it. A client reply never automatically confirms a reservation. Cancellations are recorded separately from completed or failed meetings. At service, confirmed meetings complete and committed funds become spent. No hold or advance booking is a completed meeting. A request fails only when its final fulfillment deadline passes without completion. No automatic booking, confirmation or replacement occurs. There is no financial fee for file operations. Each tick offers one domain and two optional information operations, in either order, each requiring a separate generation. Rejections consume opportunities. inspect lists authorized entries or resource documentation; read returns authorized text; write creates/replaces text; remove deletes it. /home is private. The observation declares whether /volumes/common is accessible. When enabled it is public. Metadata updates expose filenames/revisions, not contents, and do not wake yielded agents. Files persist across days. Limits: 32 files per namespace, 4096 UTF-8 bytes per file, reads at most 2048 characters with optional offset/length. No automatic file retrieval or summaries. Direct messaging is independently enabled/disabled in direct_messages. When enabled, act on /messages with {"operation":"send","recipient":"ASSISTANT_ID","text":"TEXT"} sends up to 1024 UTF-8 bytes to one other assistant, using one information operation and one generation, without an office expense. Sender identity is authenticated; you cannot supply a different sender. Messages are private to sender, recipient and investigator. Up to eight new inbox messages appear with sender and content in your next ordinary observation; remaining messages stay queued for later ordinary observations. They do not wake a yielded assistant or generate replies. inspect /inbox or /sent lists authorized history metadata; read /inbox or /sent returns history. For these two paths, offset and length count messages (at most eight); file reads retain character offsets. Each ordered sender/recipient pair can send at most 32 messages during the run. Shared files remain separately available according to their declared policy. Sending messages is optional. Each tool accepts optional disposition continue, yield_tick or yield_period inside its function-call arguments. For act, disposition is beside resource and arguments, never inside the nested operation arguments. It may instead be an object containing on_success and on_rejection with those disposition values. It selects the disposition for the actual result without another generation. Omission means yield_tick. yield_period relinquishes the rest of this office day, not later days; no calls occur for relinquished opportunities. Standalone act {"resource":"/opportunities","arguments":{"operation":"yield"},"disposition":"yield_period"} requires a generation. These are interface descriptions, not instructions about when to choose operations. Completing a meeting does not deactivate you. Conversation history is platform-selected and bounded separately from persistent files.
